clue.text: Restrain obstinate beast biting a couple of Zulus

indicators.note: a beast biting something holds it between its jaws, so one piece closes round another

parts.note: Zulu is Z in the radio alphabet, and a couple means two of them

explanation.surface: A handler subdues a stubborn animal that has sunk its teeth into two African tribesmen.
explanation.definitionFit: To muzzle someone is to silence or hold them back, a figurative sense of strapping up an animal's mouth.

clue.text: Flowering plant everyone cut round the edges

indicators.note: one word sits round another, forming its edges on both sides

parts.note: to mow grass is to cut it

explanation.surface: Gardening advice: everybody should trim a flowering plant around its borders.
explanation.definitionFit: Mallows are a family of herbs and shrubs grown for their pink or purple blooms.

clue.text: Persian prophet raised lightweight chicken for cooking

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word makes it read from bottom to top

parts.note: oz is the abbreviation for ounce, a small weight
a roaster is a bird reared for roasting

explanation.surface: Someone brought up a small chicken intended for the oven.
explanation.definitionFit: Zoroaster, also called Zarathustra, founded the ancient Iranian religion Zoroastrianism.

clue.text: City shelter succeeded, having duke involved

indicators.note: involved means taken inside, so the abbreviation for duke goes into the other letters

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
D is the abbreviation for duke
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: A city's refuge project worked once an aristocrat got on board.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, in northern England.

clue.text: Heavenly food provided by male relative in vast continent

indicators.note: in places the preceding pieces inside the word for the continent

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for male

explanation.surface: Divine cuisine supplied by a brother somewhere in a huge continent.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth ambrosia was what the gods ate, granting them immortality.

clue.text: Unusually slim models see English girls in Paris

indicators.note: unusually says the letters appear in an unusual order and must be rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Remarkably thin fashion models spot some young French women.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesdemoiselles is the French plural for unmarried young women, the plural form of mademoiselle.

clue.text: Share drink? That's the thinking

parts.note: a ration is a fixed share

explanation.surface: Someone proposes splitting a beverage and explains the idea behind it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying reasoning or justification for a course of action.

clue.text: Throw out injured member's supporter

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to throw it away
second meaning: a cloth loop that holds up a hurt arm

explanation.surface: A club expels a member who is hurt, along with their loyal fan.
explanation.walkthrough: Member here is a limb, not someone in a club.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means hurl or chuck; as a noun it is the bandage cradling a broken arm.

clue.text: Old cow marshal observed at foot of tree

indicators.note: in a down clue, at the foot of means placed below, so this piece follows the other

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground
Michel Ney was one of Napoleon's marshals

explanation.surface: A military marshal is seen standing beneath a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alderney was a breed of dairy cattle from the Channel Island of that name, now extinct.

clue.text: Elderly noblewoman's bet daughter unveiled at first during party game

indicators.note: during places these pieces inside the event formed by the last two words

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter

indicators.note: at first keeps only the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: An old aristocrat places a wager while her daughter is revealed during a parlour game.
explanation.walkthrough: Party game reads as one thing, but the party and the game are separate words, opened up so the middle pieces fit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager duchess is the widow of a duke, keeping her title after his heir marries.

clue.text: Liable to pinch uncle's oar somehow?

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: Is someone inclined to steal their uncle's rowing paddle?
explanation.walkthrough: Pinch is British slang for steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Larcenous describes someone given to larceny, the legal term for theft.

clue.text: Combination of notes, one used in a form of jazz

indicators.note: used in puts the numeral inside the jazz style

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A chord appears in a style of jazz music.
explanation.definitionFit: A triad is a three-note chord built from a root, third and fifth.

clue.text: Eggs on violent activists to begin with

indicators.note: to begin with keeps only the opening letter of each of the words

parts.note: the opening letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Someone eggs on militant protesters at the start of a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: Eggs on reads as urges, but the definition is just Eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: Ova is the Latin plural of ovum, a female reproductive cell.

clue.text: Alarmist in Greece mostly involved with Romans

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped
involved means tangled together, so the letters get mixed up

parts.note: the country with its last letter removed

explanation.surface: A doom-monger in Greece is mostly mixed up with the people of Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: A scaremonger spreads frightening rumours, much as an alarmist raises needless fears.

clue.text: Figure standing briefly at end of lane

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes
end of keeps only the final letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A figure stands for a moment at the end of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure of a person or animal, typically life-size.

clue.text: Pamphlet cleverly put together in a manageable way

parts.note: a tract is a short pamphlet

explanation.surface: A leaflet has been assembled smartly so it is easy to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tractably means compliantly, in the way of something docile and easily controlled.

clue.text: Old woman ditches union leader, getting shot?

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old

indicators.note: to ditch something is to get rid of it, so a letter is removed
the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

explanation.surface: An elderly woman drops her trade union boss and gets fired.
explanation.walkthrough: Shot suggests a gun, but here it is the adjective for silk that shimmers in changing colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot fabric changes colour with the light, which is the iridescent sheen of opal.

clue.text: Resentful granny finally hurt by current jibe

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side

parts.note: nan is a name for a grandmother

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A grandmother is at last wounded by a topical insult.
explanation.walkthrough: Current tempts the electrical AC or I, but here it means fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Indignant means angry at perceived unfairness, the same feeling as resentment.

clue.text: Not fair, coach being out of sight of the house

definitions.text: out of sight of the house

parts.note: something a bit off is unfair or unacceptable

explanation.surface: It is unfair that the bus is parked where no one in the house can see it.
explanation.walkthrough: The house is a theatre audience, not a home.
explanation.definitionFit: Offstage action happens in the wings, hidden from the audience in the auditorium.

clue.text: Presumptuous president once torn apart by conflict

indicators.note: torn apart means split open, with the other word filling the gap

parts.note: Gerald Ford was a US president

explanation.surface: An overbearing former president is ripped apart by warfare.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward can mean bold or overfamiliar, behaving with too much confidence.

clue.text: In run-down environment, finally keep fast

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the surrounding word

parts.note: seedy means shabby and run-down; environment marks it as the surrounding piece

indicators.note: finally keeps only the closing letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: In a shabby setting someone at last manages to fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Fast looks like a verb about not eating; it is the adjective for quick.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedy is a direct synonym of fast, moving quickly.

clue.text: Tropical tree some accommodated in bar

indicators.note: accommodated in means housed inside the other word

explanation.surface: A tropical tree has some people staying in a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The banyan is an Indian fig whose aerial roots grow into extra trunks.

clue.text: Sensational act clears up messes

indicators.note: something messed about is jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dazzling performance tidies up a chaotic situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Spectacular means impressively striking or dramatic, causing great excitement.

clue.text: Welshman has change of heart, finding betting odds

indicators.note: the middle letter of the name is swapped for a different one

parts.note: Evans is a very common Welsh surname

explanation.surface: A man from Wales changes his mind after looking at the odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Evens are odds of one to one, where a winning stake is doubled.

clue.text: In Mauritius ready to regret restricting exercise

indicators.note: restricting means hemming something in on both sides

explanation.surface: Someone on Mauritius is prepared to be sorry they ever took up workouts.
explanation.walkthrough: Ready is British slang for cash, as in the readies.
explanation.definitionFit: The rupee is the currency of Mauritius, as of India and Pakistan.

clue.text: Dynamic type on radio in part of India

indicators.note: on the radio words are heard, not seen, so the sound counts

parts.note: a goer is a lively, energetic person

explanation.surface: An energetic person broadcasts from a region of India.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a small state on the west coast of India, once a Portuguese colony.

clue.text: One primarily relishing beer — bitter

parts.note: an ace is the one in cards or dice

indicators.note: primarily keeps the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: the first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone above all enjoys a pint of bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter suggests the British beer, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Acerb is a rare form of acerbic, meaning sour or harsh in taste or tone.

clue.text: Model former politician protecting key city transport

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, keeping the next piece inside

parts.note: ex means former and MP is a Member of Parliament
RY is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: A one-time MP guards the key to the city's transport network.
explanation.definitionFit: Exemplary means serving as a model, an example others should follow.

clue.text: Lamb possibly? Try it without sauce initially

indicators.note: without means outside, so one piece wraps round another
initially keeps only the first letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A cook suggests tasting lamb plain, with no sauce at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia; the question mark flags him as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb was a celebrated English writer of personal essays, so he is one example of the type.

clue.text: Jam ingredient originally exported in copper container

indicators.note: in places that single letter inside the police abbreviation

parts.note: a copper is a police constable, PC

indicators.note: originally keeps only the first letter of the word after it

explanation.surface: A jam ingredient was first shipped abroad in a copper vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests the metal Cu; here it is British slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Pectin is the natural setting agent in fruit that makes jam gel.
